chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abd al-Rahman from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Ali (peace be upon him) performed the obligatory Tawaf for eight circuits; he left seven and built upon one, and added six to it. Then he prayed two rak'ahs behind the Maqam. Then he went out to As-Safa and Al-Marwah. When he finished the Sa'y between them, he returned and prayed two rak'ahs for what he had left in the first Maqam.

And whoever remembers in the eighth circuit, before reaching the Rukn, that he has performed seven circuits, let him cut off the Tawaf. And if he does not remember until he passes it, he completes fourteen circuits.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one realizes they missed a circuit during Tawaf before or after reaching the Rukn?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via Zurarah, clarifies the specific mechanics of Tawaf correction, emphasizing the distinction between realizing an error before or after passing the Rukn al-Hajar. It highlights the scholarly principle of 'building upon' the valid portion rather than restarting, reflecting the practical jurisprudence (fiqh) of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding ritual precision and ease.
